title: One
body:
A moment of solitude on the balcony of a house in a village near Sitia, where nothing but natural sounds could be heard, was enough to make me realize that I have gloriously taken part in an eternal, global feast.

Facing me on an electric pole, I observe a gecko silently, patiently, and with total focus stalking behind an unidentified insect that is heading upward, likely searching for its evening meal, while simultaneously feeling under a persistent raid of mosquitoes and gnats continuously targeting my sweet blood, which I had just charged with the sugar of the fruit drink that happened to be in the fridge, at the exact same time I'm trying to peel a firiki apple I found on the kitchen counter—and eventually abandoned because I noticed a hole from a little worm that had obviously discovered it before me.

And that is how fellow-feeders [syn-trofoi] the imperfect creation moves. Always chasing after something you lack and the other possesses. And this happens within the bounds of an endless futility, which makes me wonder: if we were indeed One, would we find our completeness and thereby escape the pain of need? Or does this condition prove beyond a doubt that everything is One?
And I speak of the Uni-verse [Syn-pan].

y.f.
